answer: An agent network can require every new identity to lock a scarce token before gaining voting weight, with influence released only gradually as the account participates. One person can wait and build a record, but a sybil attacker must lock more capital for longer across many accounts. If funding flows spiral from one source, a pulse of linked registrations can trigger review before they vote, protecting the terrace of established identities. The deposit does not prove personhood; it makes mass impersonation costly and slow.
